questions.question: What does Excalidraw do, and who runs or embeds it?
questions.answer: It is a virtual hand-drawn-style whiteboard. Browser users run excalidraw.com; application developers embed the React editor npm package. The hosted app adds collaboration, encryption and local-first storage; those app features must not all be attributed to the editor package.
requiredFacts: Hand-drawn-style whiteboard
Browser users run the hosted app
Developers embed the React npm editor
Hosted-app features are distinguished from package capabilities

evidence.excerpt:
An open source virtual hand-drawn style whiteboard.
Collaborative and end-to-end encrypted.

The Excalidraw editor (npm package) supports:

- 💯 Free & open-source.
- 🎨 Infinite, canvas-based whiteboard.
- ✍️ Hand-drawn like style.
- 🌓 Dark mode.
- 🏗️ Customizable.
- 📷 Image support.
- 😀 Shape libraries support.
- 🌐 Localization (i18n) support.
- 🖼️ Export to PNG, SVG & clipboard.
- 💾 Open format - export drawings as an `.excalidraw` json file.
- ⚒️ Wide range of tools - rectangle, circle, diamond, arrow, line, free-draw, eraser...
- ➡️ Arrow-binding & labeled arrows.
- 🔙 Undo / Redo.
- 🔍 Zoom and panning support.

## Excalidraw.com

The app hosted at [excalidraw.com](https://excalidraw.com) is a minimal showcase of what you can build with Excalidraw. Its [source code](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/tree/master/excalidraw-app) is part of this repository as well, and the app features:

- 📡 PWA support (works offline).
- 🤼 Real-time collaboration.
- 🔒 End-to-end encryption.
- 💾 Local-first support (autosaves to the browser).
- 🔗 Shareable links (export to a readonly link you can share with others).

We'll be adding these features as drop-in plugins for the npm package in the future.

**Note:** following instructions are for installing the Excalidraw [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@excalidraw/excalidraw) when integrating Excalidraw into your own app. To run the repository locally for development, please refer to our [Development Guide](https://docs.excalidraw.com/docs/introduction/development).

Use `npm` or `yarn` to install the package.

```bash
npm install react react-dom @excalidraw/excalidraw
# or
yarn add react react-dom @excalidraw/excalidraw
```

Check out our [documentation](https://docs.excalidraw.com/docs/@excalidraw/excalidraw/installation) for more details!

questions.question: Name the principal Excalidraw components and their responsibilities.
questions.answer: excalidraw-app is the hosted showcase application; packages/excalidraw exposes the embeddable React editor; packages/element holds element-related logic; packages/math supplies math functions. Equivalent package names are accepted. These are concrete components, not an inferred runtime hierarchy.
requiredFacts: excalidraw-app is the hosted application
packages/excalidraw exposes the React editor
packages/element provides element logic
packages/math provides math functions

questions.question: Which languages, framework/build systems and package boundaries organize Excalidraw?
questions.answer: TypeScript/TSX and React organize editor source. A private Yarn 1 workspace spans excalidraw-app, packages/* and examples/*; package-local build scripts are orchestrated at the root. Vite and Vitest are declared for app tooling/testing and tsc for typechecking. Workspace manifests, not arbitrary directories, define package boundaries.
requiredFacts: TypeScript/TSX with React
Yarn workspaces include app, packages and examples
Vite/Vitest and TypeScript tools are declared
Separate package build scripts exist

questions.question: Where does public-library use of restoreElements begin?
questions.answer: The editor public entry packages/excalidraw/index.tsx reexports restoreElements from ./data/restore. Its implementation is the exported generic restoreElements in packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts, receiving target elements, optional existing context, and restoration options. This is a library API entry, not a browser executable main.
requiredFacts: Public index reexports restoreElements
Definition is in data/restore.ts
Inputs are target elements, existing context and options
Library entry is not executable startup

questions.question: Where is X = detecting invisibly small elements implemented, and what qualifies?
questions.answer: packages/element/src/sizeHelpers.ts defines isInvisiblySmallElement. Linear/free-draw elements are small with fewer than two points, or with exactly two points when an arrow has endpoints equal within the 0.1 threshold passed to pointsEqual. Other element kinds require both width and height equal to zero. It is not a general area threshold.
requiredFacts: Definition is isInvisiblySmallElement in packages/element/src/sizeHelpers.ts
Linear/free-draw fewer than two points qualifies
Two-point arrows compare endpoints using threshold 0.1
Other kinds require width and height both zero

questions.question: Which internal packages does A = @excalidraw/element directly declare as dependencies, and what proves the direction?
questions.answer: packages/element/package.json declares dependencies on @excalidraw/common, @excalidraw/math and @excalidraw/fractional-indexing. Each edge is element -> named dependency. This is manifest dependency evidence, not proof that every element function calls all three.
requiredFacts: element -> common
element -> math
element -> fractional-indexing
dependencies entries prove package direction, not universal execution

questions.question: For R = restore a supported invisible rectangle with deleteInvisibleElements=true, trace the source path to its outcome and identify boundaries.
questions.answer: restoreElements reduces targetElements, skips legacy selection elements, calls restoreElement, and for a successfully migrated element calls isInvisiblySmallElement on the original element. A true result causes bumpVersion and a copy with isDeleted:true, then pushes it into the result and syncInvalidIndices normalizes indices. With repairBindings absent it returns that result. It marks a tombstone rather than filtering the item out. Invalid/failed restoreElement results are omitted; element-type migration and optional binding repair are separate branches, not universal steps.
requiredFacts: restoreElements calls restoreElement before the invisibility check
Check is gated by deleteInvisibleElements and successful migration
True causes bumpVersion and isDeleted:true
Marked element remains in array; syncInvalidIndices runs
Optional repairBindings and failed migration are distinguished

questions.question: If Y = isInvisiblySmallElement changes, which direct consumers in restore.ts and element/index.ts are evidenced, and what impact is only inferred?
questions.answer: restoreElements directly calls the helper when deleteInvisibleElements is enabled; getVisibleElements directly calls it in a filter after isNonDeletedElement. The editor public index also reexports the helper, which is exposure rather than invocation. Restoration tombstone decisions and visible-element filtering may change, but this does not prove every UI/render/export path executes either consumer.
requiredFacts: restoreElements directly invokes the helper conditionally
getVisibleElements directly invokes the helper while filtering
Public reexport is not a call
Wider runtime impact remains conditional

questions.question: Which test exercises X through restoration, and what does its mocking limit?
questions.answer: packages/excalidraw/tests/data/restore.test.ts spies on the package helper. The test named should return empty array when isInvisiblySmallElement is true actually mocks true, invokes restore.restoreElements with deleteInvisibleElements:true, and expects an element with isDeleted:true. Despite the stale test title, it proves intended tombstone wiring, not the real geometric predicate because that predicate is mocked.

Helper is spied on and mocked true
restoreElements receives deleteInvisibleElements:true
Assertion retains an isDeleted:true element
Mocked predicate does not test real geometry

questions.question: Where does Z = deleteInvisibleElements restoration option enter and get transformed into deletion state?
questions.answer: It enters the opts parameter of restoreElements. It is forwarded to restoreElement and separately gates isInvisiblySmallElement; a successful match bumps version then creates a migrated-element copy with isDeleted:true. Absent/false does not activate that caller-side deletion branch. The original element is used for the smallness predicate.
requiredFacts: Option declared on restoreElements opts
Forwarded into restoreElement
Gates predicate on original element
Result becomes bumped-version isDeleted:true migrated element
